result.answer:
Verdict: NOT ENOUGH EVIDENCE

- Evidence for: IL-4 and IL-13 abrogated autophagy and autophagy-mediated killing of intracellular mycobacteria in murine and human macrophages, and Th2 cytokines affected macrophage control of intracellular M. tuberculosis [S:80cc106acbd3#3].
- Gap: the supplied text concerns Th2 cytokines and autophagy, not helminth infection; it does not report helminth-driven impairment of IL-4-activated macrophages or increased M. tuberculosis replication [S:80cc106acbd3#2][S:80cc106acbd3#3].

citations.text:
[3] Here, we report that Th2 cytokines affect autophagy in macrophages and their ability to control
intracellular M. tuberculosis.
[4] IL-4 and IL-13 abrogated autophagy and autophagy-mediated killing of intracellular mycobacteria in
murine and human macrophages.
[5] Inhibition of starvation-induced autophagy by IL-4 and IL-13 was dependent on Akt signaling, whereas
the inhibition of IFN-gamma-induced autophagy was Akt independent and signal transducer and activator
of transcription 6 (STAT6) dependent.
[6] These findings establish a mechanism through which Th1-Th2 polarization differentially affects the
immune control of intracellular pathogens.
